The major product of the following reaction is :

 
[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The substrate is a secondary benzylic iodide, $\mathrm{PhS}{}^{-}$ is a strong, soft nucleophile and DMF is a polar aprotic solvent, so substitution occurs by the $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ path at the benzylic carbon.

In $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ the nucleophile attacks from the side opposite to the leaving group, so the configuration at the benzylic carbon is inverted: the wedged C–I bond is replaced by a dashed C–SPh bond.

The ring fluorine is not replaced: F is meta to the $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ group, so the anion that addition of $\mathrm{PhS}{}^{-}$ at that carbon would form cannot be stabilised by $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$, and nucleophilic aromatic substitution does not occur.


[IMG]

Option (C) shows retention, which $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ cannot give.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

Given below are two statements :

Statement I : In Hofmann degradation reaction, the migration of only an alkyl group takes place from carbonyl carbon of the amide to the nitrogen atom.

Statement II : The group is migrated in Hofmann degradation reaction to electron deficient atom.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Hofmann bromamide degradation

In this degradation, the migration of the alkyl/aryl group occurs to the electron-deficient nitrogen (nitrene).

Statement (II) is correct as the migration occurs to the electron-deficient atom.

text: L-isomer of a compound $'A' (C_{4}H_{8}O_{4})$ gives a positive test with [$Ag(NH_{3})_{2}$]$^{+}$. Treatment of 'A' with acetic anhydride yields triacetate derivative. Compound 'A' produces an optically active compound (B) and an optically inactive compound (C) on treatment with bromine water and HNO$_{3}$ respectively. Compound (A) is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{C}{}_{4}\mathrm{H}{}_{8}\mathrm{O}{}_{4}$ that reduces Tollens' reagent $[\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{2}]{}^{+}$ and forms a triacetate is an aldotetrose, $\mathrm{CHO}-\mathrm{CHOH}-\mathrm{CHOH}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}$, with three $-\mathrm{OH}$ groups.

Bromine water oxidises only $-\mathrm{CHO}$ to $-\mathrm{COOH}$. The product $\mathrm{HOOC}-\mathrm{CHOH}-\mathrm{CHOH}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}$ has two different ends, so it stays chiral and optically active (B).

Nitric acid oxidises both $-\mathrm{CHO}$ and $-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}$ to $-\mathrm{COOH}$, giving tartaric acid (C). It is optically inactive only as meso-tartaric acid, which needs the two $-\mathrm{OH}$ groups on the same side of the Fischer projection, so the sugar is erythrose, not threose.

In the L-isomer the $-\mathrm{OH}$ on the stereocentre farthest from $-\mathrm{CHO}$ is on the left, so L-erythrose has both $-\mathrm{OH}$ groups on the left, which is structure (A).


[IMG]


[IMG]

Structure (C) is D-erythrose, which also gives meso-tartaric acid but is the D-isomer; (B) and (D) are threoses, which give optically active tartaric acid.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift

text:
If the uncertainty in velocity and position of a minute particle in space are, 2.4 $\times$ $10^{-26} (m s^{-1})$ and $10^{-7} (m)$ respectively. The mass of the particle in g is $____________. ($Nearest integer)

(Given : h = 6.626 $\times$ $10^{-34} Js)$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know from Heisenberg uncertainty principle

$\Delta x.\Delta p=\frac{h}{4π}$

$\Rightarrow \Delta x.m\Delta v=\frac{h}{4π}$

Given, 

$\Delta x = 10^{-7} m$

$\Delta$v = 2.4 $\times$ $10^{-26} m/s$

h = 6.626 $\times$ $10^{-34} Js$

$\therefore$ $10^{-7}\times m\times 2.4\times 10^{-26}=\frac{6.626\times 10^{-34}}{4π}$

$\Rightarrow 2.4m=\frac{6.626}{4π\times 10}$

$\Rightarrow$ m = 0.022 kg

$\Rightarrow$ m = 22 gm
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift

2NOCl(g) $⇌$ $2NO(g) + Cl_{2}(g)$

In an experiment, 2.0 moles of NOCl was placed in a one-litre flask and the concentration of NO after equilibrium established, was found to be 0.4 mol/L. The equilibrium constant at 30${}^{\circ }$C is $______________$ $\times$ $10^{-4}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Given that at equilibrium, concentration of NO = 0.4 mol/L

$\therefore$ 2x = 0.4

$\Rightarrow$ x = 0.2

$\therefore$ Concentration of NOCl at equilibrium,

[NOCl]$_{eq} = 2$ $-$ 2 $\times$ 0.2 = 1.6

and [NO]$_{eq} = 0.4$

and [$Cl_{2}$]$_{eq} = 0.2$

We know,

$K_{C}=\frac{[NO]^{2}[Cl_{2}]}{[NOCl]^{2}}$

$=\frac{[0.4]^{2}[0.2]}{[1.6]^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow K_{C}=12.5\times 10^{-3}$

$\Rightarrow K_{C}=125\times 10^{-4}$

text:
The number of statements correct from the following for Copper (at. no. 29) is/are $____________$.

(A) Cu(II) complexes are always paramagnetic.

(B) Cu(I) complexes are generally colourless

(C) Cu(I) is easily oxidized

(D) In Fehling solution, the active reagent has Cu(I)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(A) $\mathrm{Cu}$ (II) complexes are always paramagnetic as they have one unpaired electron due to $d^{9}$ configuration of $\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{II})$

(B) $\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{I})$ complexes are generally colourless due to $d^{10}$ configuration.

(C) $\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{I})$ is easily oxidised to $\mathrm{Cu}^{+2}$ in aqueous solution

$2\mathrm{Cu}^{+}\to \mathrm{Cu}^{+2}+\mathrm{Cu}$

$\mathrm{Cu}^{+1}$ disproportionates to $\mathrm{Cu}^{+2}$ and $\mathrm{Cu}$

$\left (E_{\text{cell}}^{\circ }>0 \right.$ for this cell reaction in aqueous solution)

In Fehling's solution, active reagent has $\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{II})$ which is reduced to $\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{I})$ on reaction with aldehydes.

Hence (D) statement is incorrect
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift

text: Acidified potassium permanganate solution oxidises oxalic acid. The spin-only magnetic moment of the manganese product formed from the above reaction is $____________ B.M. ($Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{KMnO}_{4}$ (acidic medium) $+\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}\to \mathrm{CO}_{2}+\mathrm{Mn}^{+2}$

 $\mathrm{Mn}^{+2}$ has 5 unpaired electrons

$\therefore$ Spin only magnetic moment $=\sqrt{5(5+2)}$

$\begin{array}{l} =\sqrt{5\times 7} \\  \\ =\sqrt{35} \\  \\ \simeq 5.92\text{B.M.} \\  \\ \simeq 6\text{B.M.} \end{array}$

text: Two elements A and B which form 0.15 moles of $A_{2}B$ and $AB_{3}$ type compounds. If both $A_{2}B$ and $AB_{3}$ weigh equally, then the atomic weight of A is $_____________$ times of atomic weight of B.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let atomic weight of A = x

and atomic weight of B = y

$\therefore$ Molar mass of $A_{2}B = 2x + y$

and molar mass of $AB_{3} = x + 3y$

Now, weight of 0.15 moles of $A_{2}B = (2x + y) 0.15$

and weight of 0.15 moles of $AB_{3} = (x + 3y) 0.15$

Given, weight of 0.15 moles of $A_{2}B$ and $AB_{3}$ are equal.

$\therefore$ (2x + y)0.15 = (x + 3y)0.15

$\Rightarrow$ x = 2y

$\Rightarrow \frac{x}{y}=2$

$\therefore$ Atomic weight of A is 2 times of atomic weight of B.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift

text: Total number of possible stereoisomers of dimethyl cyclopentane is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The positional isomers are 1,1-, 1,2- and 1,3-dimethylcyclopentane.

1,1-Dimethylcyclopentane has no stereocentre and no cis–trans relationship, so it has no stereoisomers.

1,2-Dimethylcyclopentane has two stereocentres: the cis form has a plane of symmetry and is meso, and the trans form is chiral and exists as the enantiomers $(1R,2R)$ and $(1S,2S)$, giving 3 stereoisomers.

1,3-Dimethylcyclopentane likewise gives a meso cis form and the trans enantiomers $(1R,3R)$ and $(1S,3S)$, giving 3 stereoisomers.

Total number of stereoisomers $=3+3=6$.

Hence, the answer is 6.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift
